Sign out of an extension's account

extensions.languageModelAccess.description: Let extensions use your language model (VS Code's lm API: an extension's own AI features, its chat participants). Each extension still asks once. Off: they find no model.

extensions.languageModelAllowed.description: Extensions you allowed to use your language model (while extensions.languageModelAccess is on).

extensions.typeOverride.acknowledged.description: Extensions you kept handling what you type in the editor (a Vim keymap): the notice isn't shown for them again.

extensions.typeOverride.blocked.description: Extensions that may not handle what you type in the editor (the notice's Turn off adds them).

extensions.store.enabled.description: Search, install and update VS Code extensions from Open VSX (open-vsx.org) in the Extensions view: their themes, icon themes, grammars, snippets and settings work. Only fetched when you search, install, check for updates (extensions.autoCheckUpdates: a minute after start, with extensions from Open VSX installed) or open an extension's page, and for the Recommended section while the view is shown; downloads are checked against Open VSX's SHA-256. Off: the view filters installed extensions only.

extensions.autoUpdate.description: Update VS Code extensions from Open VSX by themselves: a minute after the IDE starts it asks Open VSX for newer versions and installs them. An extension's own Auto update choice (its page or its menu) wins over this.

extensions.updateDelayHours.description: How long a new version of a VS Code extension has to be out on Open VSX before it's offered as an update (by itself or in the notice): a version published by mistake or by someone who took over the account is usually pulled by then. Meanwhile the newest version that's old enough is offered. 0 offers each version at once. Installing a specific version isn't held back.

extensions.autoCheckUpdates.description: When VS Code extensions from Open VSX are installed, check for newer versions a minute after the IDE starts: a notice offers to update them, and the Extensions icon shows how many. Nothing is installed unless you choose to (or turn on extensions.autoUpdate).

extensions.recommendations.enabled.description: Show a Recommended section in the Extensions view: extensions the workspace's .vscode/extensions.json names, and well-known ones for its kinds of files (Python, Go, Rust, Docker…). Their details come from Open VSX while the view is shown (with extensions.store.enabled on).

extensions.recommendations.ignored.description: Extensions no longer recommended (the Recommended section's Ignore adds them).

extensions.officialRepo.description: The repository of official extensions (owner/name on GitHub, or a git URL) that Browse official extensions lists. Empty: the IDE's own, once there is one.
